Yes, all octopuses — not just most — are venomous [d1][d8]. According to Wikipedia, "All octopuses are venomous, but only the blue-ringed octopuses are known to be deadly to humans" [d1]. A peer-reviewed source from NCBI confirms that common octopuses "possess digestive enzymes and neurotoxins in glands connected to their horny beak and may use this venom for defense or to subdue prey," with blue-ringed octopus venom containing tetrodotoxin and common octopus venom containing cephalotoxin [d2]. Multiple other sources reinforce this: OctoNation notes that "ALL octopuses are venomous but only two contain the lethal TTX (the Blue-Ringed Octopus and the Mototi Octopus)" [d6], and Golden's wiki states "all octopuses have venom, not all of them are dangerous to humans" [d7]. While all octopuses are venomous, most species' venom is not harmful to humans, and octopuses are generally not aggressive toward people [d4][d8].
